after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To express the number in Cartesian form, we expand the parentheses and substitute the values of the cosine and sine.

Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )=-1$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =5(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )) \\  & =5(-1+\text{i}\cdot 0) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Rationalizing gives z = 4(1+i)/2 = 2+2i. Its modulus is √(2²+2²) = 2√2, and its argument is π/4 because it lies in the first quadrant with equal real and imaginary parts.

after.worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1+\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{4}{1-\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{(1-\text{i})(1+\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{1+1} \\  & =2(1+\text{i}) \\  & =2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

 

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=2+2\text{i},$ the magnitude is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

    

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=2$ and $y=2$ are both positive, $z$ lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=2\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))
$$

In polar form, r represents the magnitude |z|. For a complex number z=x+yi, the magnitude of z is given by |z|=x2+y2.

So, for z=2+2i, the magnitude is r=|z|=x2+y2=22+22=22.

In polar form, θ represents the argument arg⁡(z). Since x=2 and y=2 are both positive, z lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find θ as follows: θ=arg⁡(z)=arctan⁡(yx)=arctan⁡(22)=arctan⁡1=π4

Finally, we write the complex number z in polar form: z=22(cos⁡(π4)+isin⁡(π4))

content.worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1+\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{4}{1-\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{(1-\text{i})(1+\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4(1+\text{i})}{1+1} \\  & =2(1+\text{i}) \\  & =2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

 

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=2+2\text{i},$ the magnitude is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

    

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=2$ and $y=2$ are both positive, $z$ lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=2\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1-\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{2\text{i}}{1+\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}-2{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\text{i}+2}{1+1} \\  & =1+\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=1+\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=1$ and $y=1$ are both positive, $z$ lies in the first quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}))
$$
